decisions.reason: As a space navigation and observation camera with its own product page across both years, it fits the firm's established optical-space competencies and gives management enough related knowledge to keep improving it rather than withdraw it.
The modular space navigation camera is strongly validated by the ESA HERA launch reference and sits directly in the firm's core knowledge base, so management would almost certainly retain it.

A space situational awareness sensor suite broadens the firm's existing space-optics portfolio in a related way, and its continued standalone presentation suggests sufficient strategic value to keep it on the market.

The miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor is only mentioned rather than prominently marketed, which raises some risk, but it still builds on adjacent sensing capabilities that a large experienced firm can absorb and develop further.

A radiation-hard space camera is highly consistent with the firm's accumulated expertise in ruggedized optical systems, and a dedicated page in its launch year indicates clear commitment to commercial refinement.

The asteroid navigation and imaging camera is more niche and only lightly presented so far, but because it is closely related to the firm's proven space-camera knowledge, management is more likely to continue learning from it than to drop it quickly.
